target_customer: Professionals, founders and event organizers who want warm introductions and pre-scheduled meetings (individual subscriptions and per-event conference pricing)
problem: Finding the right people to meet for business is left to chance, cold outreach and conference wandering. Namecard.ai uses AI to match people by stated needs and offers.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: free tier, $49 per month Professional plan, per-event conference pricing of $199 to $299 (company site)
product_category: AI professional networking and event matchmaking

founders.name: Ernie Ho
education: Grad student, CMU School of Computer Science
previous_startups: Yamkr (social app that received an acquisition offer)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page for Chainsight, the sibling listing of the same team.

founders.name: John Lin
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC launch post (Ernie and John from Chainsight); no background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching profiles with embeddings and a generative AI interface was standard engineering in 2022, with the main work in data and network building.

defensibility.rationale: The company claims a network of over one million professionals, but matching and scheduling features are copyable and competitors in event networking already existed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No sourced evidence of incumbents copying it; the company remains active as of 2026 per the YC listing.

market_need_then: Conference and networking matchmaking was an established category before 2022, and the company site cites low cold email response rates as the pain.

branding.domain_note: Uses namecard.ai; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident, benefit focused, short punchy headlines and direct calls to action (company site)

brand_strength.rationale: Little press or community evidence about the brand; the name is a descriptive compound shared with several unrelated business card products.

pivots.from: Chainsight, Web3 background check API (the YC launch post for this batch)
pivots.why: Not stated in sources found. The YC launch post lists Namecard.ai as the company but describes the Chainsight product, so the pivot timing is unknown.

outcome_analysis: Namecard.ai is listed as active with a small team. The YC launch post describes the Web3 background check product Chainsight, and the company site now names Chainsight Pte. Ltd. as the operator, so the team appears to have moved from crypto risk checks to AI networking. No exit, shutdown or layoff was found, and public funding information for Namecard.ai itself is absent, so the trajectory is unclear.
notes: Aggregators (Bouncewatch, VCBacked) report a $1.8M pre-seed for Chainsight in Nov 2022 from YC, Franklin Templeton and Samsung NEXT, and CB Insights reports $570K total; the Samsung NEXT post I tried to open returned 404, so none of this is recorded as a round (unverified). Third party pages claim $1M revenue in 2024 and no outside funding; low quality sources. Competitors in event matchmaking (Brella, Grip, Swapcard) existed but I found only 2026 dated pages, so the list is empty. Completeness pass: the 1.8M pre-seed (filed under the earlier product name Chainsight) rests on databases (Bouncewatch, VCBacked), while CB Insights lists only 570K total over 4 rounds. Conflict unresolved.
